mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a single month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in subsequent months are not statistically different from a pre-tightening period (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.25% in any month for 3 consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 3.0% for two consecutive months indicate disinflation, prompting market anticipation of lower future rate cuts and thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 3.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns over the next 60 days are not statistically superior to a baseline of high-inflation periods (p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL does not remain below 3.0% for more than 4 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in employment growth (PAYEMS) by more than 10,000 monthly jobs coinciding with a decline in unemployment (UNRATE below 4.0%) creates optimism about economic resilience, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10,000 and UNRATE falls below 4.0% in the same month
failure_condition: In a sample of 10 such labor events, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during neutral labor market periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month signals weakening demand, which compresses corporate earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during subsequent months remain flat or trend positive (p < 0.05), or INDPRO recovers >10% in the following quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A multi-month decline in manufacturing activity (GDPC1) below 110% of trend suggests softening demand, which increases equity risk premia and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 remains below 110% of 4-quarter moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the next 20 days are not statistically worse than during robust GDP expansion (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of RSAFS exceeds 7,000 million dollars, it indicates strong corporate demand for safe assets, signaling a risk-off environment that compresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: 3-month moving average of RSAFS > 7,000 million dollars
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the following 60 days are not statistically lower than during low-safe-asset-demand regimes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in housing starts (HOUST) by at least 5% month-over-month for two consecutive months, alongside a steady unemployment rate below 4.5%, predicts optimism about the housing recovery and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥5% for two consecutive months and UNRATE remains <4.5% in both months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during such episodes are not significantly higher than during neutral housing growth (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 6-month moving average of UNRATE falls below 3.5% and industrial production (INDPRO) remains flat for two consecutive months, it suggests a structural soft landing, reducing growth expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE 6-month MA < 3.5% AND INDPRO is flat for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in subsequent months trend positive or are not statistically different from a baseline of neutral labor market (p < 0.05).
